practiceQuestions.q: Who acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under the Constitution of India?
opts: An elected member of Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 64 and Article 89(1) of the Constitution of India explicitly state that the Vice-President of India shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the Vice-President shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 64 specifically lays down that the Vice-President shall be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States and shall not hold any other office of profit. (Note: Article 89(1) also reiterates this for Rajya Sabha, but Article 64 is the primary constitutional provision defining this role under the Vice-President's executive/legislative functions).

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha vote during the initial voting on a bill or resolution in the House?
opts: No, because he is not a member of the Rajya Sabha
Yes, only when directed by the Prime Minister
Yes, whenever there is a tie
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vice-President, who acts as the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, is not a member of the House. Therefore, he does not have a vote in the first instance. He can only exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the term of office of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President of India, whose normal term of office is 5 years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

practiceQuestions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
opts: The Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha
The senior-most member of Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: The oath of office to the Vice-President (who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha) is administered by the President of India or some person appointed in that behalf by him.

practiceQuestions.q: Under whose authority is the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha elected?
opts: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: The Rajya Sabha chooses one of its members to be the Deputy Chairman whenever the office falls vacant, and this election is conducted under the overall supervision and authority of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: What type of majority is required in the Rajya Sabha to remove its Deputy Chairman?
opts: Absolute majority of the total members
Majority of all the then members of the House
Two-thirds majority of members present and voting
Simple majority of members present and voting
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 90(c), a resolution for the removal of the Deputy Chairman must be passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha (effective majority).

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha preside over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
opts: Yes, if the Speaker of Lok Sabha is absent
Yes, by rotation with the Speaker
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 118(4), joint sittings of Parliament are presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and in their absence, by the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha, or if they are also absent, such other person as may be determined by the rules of procedure. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha never presides over a joint sitting because he is not a member of either House.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha tender his resignation if he wishes to resign?
opts: The Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President of India, he tenders his resignation to the President of India under Article 67(a).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the official title given to the casting vote exercised by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 100(1), the Chairman does not vote in the first instance, but has and can exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the framers of the Indian Constitution choose the Vice-President of India as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha instead of electing a Chairman from among its own members?
opts: To ensure absolute political neutrality and avoid partisanship in presiding over the Upper House representing federal units.
Because the Vice-President has no other constitutional duties assigned to him.
To give the Vice-President executive control over legislative drafting.
To reduce the financial burden of maintaining a separate secretariat for the Chairman.
practiceQuestions.sol: By making the Vice-President (a national figure elected by both houses) the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the framers sought to keep the office of the Chairman above party politics, ensuring a neutral, dignified custodian for the House of States.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the removal process of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha structurally differ from the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
opts: The Chairman is removed by a resolution passed by Rajya Sabha alone, while the Speaker is removed by Lok Sabha.
The Chairman can only be removed from office if he is removed from the office of Vice-President, which requires a resolution initiated in Rajya Sabha and agreed to by Lok Sabha.
The Chairman can be removed by the President directly upon the advice of the Prime Minister.
There is no difference; both are removed by a joint sitting of Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President, he cannot be removed by the Rajya Sabha alone. He can only be removed from the office of Vice-President by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a special/effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to the legislative powers and duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha when he is discharging the functions of the President under Article 65?
opts: He continues to preside over the Rajya Sabha simultaneously.
He ceases to perform the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and does not draw the salary/allowance of the Chairman during that period.
He exercises presidential veto over Rajya Sabha bills.
He delegates his casting vote to the Prime Minister.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 65(3) specifies that during any period when the Vice-President is acting as, or discharging the functions of, the President, he is not to perform the duties of the office of Chairman of the Council of States and is entitled to the salary and allowance payable to the President.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of Money Bills, what is the institutional role and limitation of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
opts: He has the sole power to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill in Rajya Sabha.
He cannot certify a Money Bill; certification is exclusively done by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and the Chairman's role is limited to managing recommendations within 14 days.
He can veto a Money Bill if it violates federal financial provisions.
He refers Money Bills to the Supreme Court for judicial review before discussion.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 110(4), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the exclusive power to certify a Money Bill. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has no certification power; the Rajya Sabha can only discuss and make recommendations on Money Bills within 14 days.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Chairman's control over the Secretariat of the Rajya Sabha function constitutionally?
opts: The Rajya Sabha Secretariat functions independently under the Union Cabinet.
The Chairman is the head of the Rajya Sabha Secretariat, exercising administrative control and appointing officers under the recruitment rules framed in consultation with him.
The Secretariat is directly managed by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
The Chairman shares administrative control equally with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

Under Article 98, each House of Parliament has a separate secretarial staff. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha heads the Rajya Sabha Secretariat and exercises supreme administrative authority over its functioning and appointments.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the Chairman's power regarding the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule) in the Rajya Sabha?
opts: The Chairman decides questions of disqualification on the ground of defection for members of the Rajya Sabha.
The Chairman refers all defection cases to the Election Commission of India for a binding verdict.
The Chairman can expel a member from Parliament for defection without a formal inquiry.
The Chairman has no jurisdiction under the Tenth Schedule; only the Supreme Court decides defection.

Under Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, questions relating to disqualification of a member of the Rajya Sabha on the ground of defection are referred for the decision of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, whose decision is subject to judicial review.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha often described as a structural bridge between the Executive and the Legislature?
opts: Because he is a member of the Union Cabinet while heading the House.
Because he holds a constitutional executive post (Vice-President) while discharging supreme legislative presiding duties in the federal House.
Because he drafts executive ordinances passed by the Rajya Sabha.
Because he appoints the Prime Minister in case of a hung Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vice-President is part of the executive branch (Executive of the Union under Part V), yet his primary statutory function is presiding over the Rajya Sabha, placing him at the unique intersection of executive and legislative branches.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha exercise authority over Parliamentary Committees of the House?
opts: He appoints all committee chairpersons, nominates members to Rajya Sabha committees, and issues directions to them regarding their functioning.
He directly audits the financial accounts investigated by the Public Accounts Committee.
He has no control over committees; they report exclusively to the Prime Minister.
He can dissolve any parliamentary committee at his personal discretion without consulting the House.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha nominates members to various standing and select committees of the House (such as the Business Advisory Committee, Committee on Privileges, etc.) and appoints their chairpersons in accordance with the rules of procedure.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional recourse if both the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are simultaneously absent during a session?
opts: The Prime Minister takes over the chairmanship temporarily.
A panel of vice-chairpersons nominated by the Chairman presides over the House according to a designated hierarchy.
The House is automatically adjourned sine die.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha conducts joint presiding duties.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 89(2), the Rajya Sabha has a panel of vice-chairpersons nominated by the Chairman. If both Chairman and Deputy Chairman are absent, a member from this panel presides, as per Rule 8 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: In the event of a deadlock between Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on a non-money bill, why does the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha not participate in the ensuing joint sitting?
opts: Because joint sittings are exclusively presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker under constitutional mandate.
Because the Chairman is legally barred from entering the Lok Sabha chamber where joint sittings are held.
Because he represents the executive and must remain neutral on legislative deadlocks.
Because he casts his vote before the joint sitting commences.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 118(4) explicitly designates the Speaker of the Lok Sabha as the presiding officer of a joint sitting of the two Houses. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has no constitutional role in a joint sitting since he is an officer of the Rajya Sabha and not a member of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. He is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
3. He can be removed from his office by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a simple majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 64 designates the Vice-President as ex-officio Chairman. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 66(1), the Vice-President is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (both elected and nominated). Statement 3 is incorrect because removal of the Vice-President requires a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha by a majority of all the then members (effective/special majority) and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, not a simple majority.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers and functions of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. He has the right to vote in the first instance in the Rajya Sabha on any legislative bill.
2. He decides on all questions relating to the disqualification of Rajya Sabha members under the Tenth Schedule.
3. He is the custodian and head of the Rajya Sabha Secretariat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Chairman does not vote in the first instance; he only exercises a casting vote in the event of a tie. Statement 2 is correct: Under the Tenth Schedule, the Chairman decides defection disqualification cases for Rajya Sabha. Statement 3 is correct: Under Article 98, he heads the Rajya Sabha Secretariat.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and Money Bills:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha only with the prior recommendation of the Chairman.
2. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha certifies whether a bill passed by the Rajya Sabha is a Money Bill.
3. The Rajya Sabha under the guidance of the Chairman must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Money Bills cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha at all; they can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: Certification of a Money Bill is done exclusively by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under Article 110(4), not the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Statement 3 is correct: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days with or without recommendations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Deputy Chairman is elected by the Rajya Sabha from amongst its members.
2. The office of the Deputy Chairman is constitutionally recognized under Article 89 of the Constitution.
3. When the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha acts as the President of India, the Deputy Chairman automatically assumes the office of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Article 89(2) provides that the Rajya Sabha shall choose a member to be Deputy Chairman. Statement 3 is incorrect: When the Chairman (Vice-President) acts as President, he stops performing the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, but the Deputy Chairman does not become the 'Chairman' of the Rajya Sabha; rather, the Deputy Chairman only performs the duties/presides over the Rajya Sabha during that period, while the constitutional office of Chairman remains held by the Vice-President who is discharging presidential functions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial emoluments and privileges of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha receives a separate salary specifically designated for the office of the Chairman in the Second Schedule.
2. The salary and allowances of the Chairman are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
3. The salary and allowances of the Chairman can be subjected to a vote of Parliament during annual budget discussions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Vice-President does not receive a salary as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; he receives a salary in his capacity as the Vice-President of India as specified by Parliament by law. Statement 2 is correct: Salaries and allowances of the Chairman are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 97. Statement 3 is incorrect: Charged expenditure is non-votable by Parliament (though it can be discussed).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha vis-a-vis the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. Unlike the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the House over which he presides.
2. Both the Chairman and the Speaker have the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill.
3. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha vacates office immediately upon the dissolution of the House, whereas the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha does not vacate office when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Chairman is the Vice-President and not a member of Rajya Sabha, while the Speaker is an elected member of Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: Only the Speaker has the power to certify a Money Bill; the Chairman does not. Statement 3 is correct: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body not subject to dissolution; hence its Chairman's office is continuous and unaffected by Lok Sabha dissolution.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the disciplinary and procedural powers of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Chairman can suspend a member of the Rajya Sabha for unruly behavior, a power derived directly from the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Rajya Sabha.
2. The Chairman has the power to adjourn the Rajya Sabha sine die or suspend a sitting in case of grave disorder.
3. The Chairman can override a constitutional amendment bill passed by the Lok Sabha by exercising his casting vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: The Chairman maintains order, can name members, suspend them as per rules, and adjourn/suspend sittings. Statement 3 is incorrect: Constitutional amendment bills require a special majority under Article 368 in both Houses separately; casting votes cannot override structural constitutional amendment requirements or substitute for actual majorities.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historical evolution and constitutional status of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The office of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha was modeled closely on the lines of the American Vice-President acting as the President of the US Senate.
2. Under the Government of India Act 1919, the President of the Council of State was initially nominated by the Governor-General, not elected.
3. The Indian Constitution permits the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha to participate in voting on all ordinary bills during normal proceedings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: The Indian model of making the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Upper House is directly inspired by the United States Constitution (where the US Vice-President is President of the Senate). Under the GoI Act 1919, the President of the Council of State was initially nominated. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Chairman cannot vote in the first instance.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding motions and resolutions concerning the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President (Chairman of Rajya Sabha) can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
2. While a resolution for his removal is under consideration in the Rajya Sabha, the Chairman can preside over the proceedings of the House.
3. The Chairman is entitled to a voice and a vote in the proceedings when a resolution for his removal is under discussion in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 67(b), a resolution for the removal of the Vice-President must be moved in the Rajya Sabha first, but it requires agreement of the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: Under Article 92(1), while a resolution for removal of the Vice-President is under consideration, the Chairman shall not preside. Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Article 92(2), the Chairman has the right to speak and otherwise take part in the proceedings of the Rajya Sabha while a removal resolution is under consideration, but he shall NOT be entitled to vote at all on such resolution (as he is not a member and has no initial vote, and casting vote rules do not apply for removal).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative and emergency roles of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Chairman has the authority to consult the Attorney General of India on parliamentary matters during a deadlock.
2. The Chairman determines the admissibility of notices for questions, motions, and resolutions in the Rajya Sabha in accordance with the rules of the House.
3. The emoluments and allowances of the Chairman are exempt from income tax under special parliamentary statutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Attorney General gives advice to the Government of India, not specifically to the Chairman of Rajya Sabha for parliamentary deadlocks. Statement 2 is correct: The Chairman has absolute authority under the rules of the House to decide the admissibility of questions, calling attention notices, and resolutions. Statement 3 is incorrect: Salaries and allowances of constitutional dignitaries like the Vice-President/Chairman are subject to income tax laws enacted by Parliament unless specifically exempted by a specific taxation exemption clause (which general salaries are not; they pay income tax as per the Income Tax Act applicable to MPs/officials).
